pr_title: Resolve nest pub/sub subscriber token refresh issues
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Create a full Credentials object (complete with refresh token, expiration time,
etc) so that the Pub/sub subscriber can handle token refreshes rather than
crashing after an hour.  While it is not ideal to have both Home Assistant and
Pub/sub handle token refresh, it significantly simplifies subscriber
troubleshooting to have it handle all credential management itself since it has no existing callback for getting
refreshed tokens.  Additionally, user reports that when credentials expire the subscriber may not notice, leading to
dropped "acks"s and duplicate delivery of events, since ACKs are best effort.

I previously attempted this change in #42947 and it did not work.  However, now it does
now so I must have not been creating the Credential correctly previously (e.g.
missing the expiry field in the parent class, which presumably causes the
client to know to refresh).  The workaround added in #43034 can likely be reverted after this change.

Updated google-nest-sdm version to v0.2.7
- See diffs: https://github.com/allenporter/python-google-nest-sdm/compare/v0.2.5...v0.2.7
- Motivation for this PR: Fixed a typo in the AbstractSubscriberFactory

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.

I am seeing duplicate events from Nest SDM, my only device is a hello doorbell, and I've an automation registered for DoorbellChime events -- from looking at the debug logs I think there was some server side error with nest, causing some state invalidation in the session, which maybe means hass could not acknowledge the message, causing it to be re-delivered, often almost 10 minutes later. There's a 👻 at the door!
I have seen this on several occasions, but only looked into the debug entries from one so far...

Thanks for the detailed report! very happy to talk through options.

A couple thoughts
- we can always drop events based on age in code like you did here
- we can recommend users do this with their max message age in subscription settings.  That is, I don't think you need any code changes to get this behavior yourself?

The question is really about what the default should be.  I leaned towards letting the user configure this in their subscription setting second because it seemed like you might want to have notifications for old events while home assistant was down.

However, when used with notifications this doesn't seem super useful.  But what is the right default cutoff? Seems like it depends a lot on the use case.  Some users for example might be furious that a 2 min 30 sec old notification was dropped about motion in their side yard.

Another option is we can do better dupe tracking, keeping a cache of recently observed event IDs so we don't redeliver anything.

Maybe there are other subscriber settings we can look at also to be more resilient.  I wouldn't expect that restarting the subscriber should cause previously asked messages to be delivered again, unless you're saying the messages were not in fact ACKd due to some other error.

Agreed it does depend on the use case, for a doorbell press, the person probably left after 2 minutes if they didn't start banging on the door, but for others you may still want the notification indeed.
This is why I chose to, for now, propagate the nest event time stamp into the hass event, then each automation can act as they see fit. I can share the patch for this, it's just a one line change.

The ID tracking is an interesting idea, but, I wonder where to keep that cache; if it was in memory, I can guess at a situation where hass gets restarted and the duplicate event is re-delivered and would then be acted on in duplicate.

As far as I can tell from the Google side of things, I cannot configure it to not re-send unacknowledged messages, and the minimum retention duration is 10 minutes (wonder if that's related to re-delivery time 🤔)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/431228/103237367-45568f00-493f-11eb-9e43-0f5d60971f9d.jpeg)

Ah didn't realize there was a minimum.  Adding the timestamp to the event seems perfectly reasonable, and potentially useful.  Happy to review such a PR, or can do the leg work of copying your implementation if you want to give a pointer to save some time.

I think there may still be worth digging into trying to make redelivery less likely, so maybe we can dig into that a bit more here. 
  It makes me think that the current approach of restarting the stream when noticing invalid creds is not sufficient.

The context here is that we're using OAuth tokens that need to be regularly refreshed.  However, I don't think the python library supports fetching new credentials on a regular interval.   In https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/42993 was the first attempt, to make this use long lived credentials from a service account as a workaround, but we decided instead to make the [subscriber restart](https://github.com/allenporter/python-google-nest-sdm/commit/94ee42f76a33ff0ed2f5a0397b42e59ba03aace9#diff-2017e6864c9da4b17f6520596d5b940421a686c489c87510e2256f2b5a9d5076) in the google-nest-sdm python library.  The current behavior is to sleep for 10 seconds, and the restart the subscriber with a watchdog that looks for the whole subscriber to fail overall.   

Do you see evidence of that happening in the log?  It almost seems like the individual "unary RPC" ACKs were failing but the overall stream receiving was not failing.

I don't have any instances of "Subscriber shut down; restarting" -- is that what I should be looking for?
It is indeed strange, new messages continue coming through despite the unauthenticated state.

It can then be used within an automation e.g.:
`now()|as_timestamp - trigger.event.data.timestamp|as_timestamp < 60*2`

I have another idea for this: The current approach is to just restart the subscriber when we notice it fails, but alternatively we can track the expiration time explicitly and set an alarm to restart it when we know the creds are going to have expired.  That seems a little more direct, and may reduce the likely hood of the subscriber hanging on to bad creds in the background.

https://github.com/googleapis/python-pubsub/issues/271

Yes. I've updated the pydoc on the method to give some context on the usage.  Let me know if that comment makes it more clear.

That is, I want to make it clear that we have two parallel paths for refreshing OAuth tokens that are happening:
- HomeAssistant manages token refresh for the API based calls.  This typically should just happen once on startup for the initial device fetch.
- Subscriber manages token refresh for the Subscriber based calls.  This will be refreshed in the background as the subscriber streaming rpcs happen.

 This current approach seems to strike a balance compared to alternatives (e.g.  switch to using Google's Auth library for the API calls to, so that it manages its own token refresh).  If you have ideas for how to unify/simplify/improve let me know.
As long as Home Assistant can still update the token as needed when setting up the integration, it seems ok.
